Cyber Solidarity Act

Regulation (EU) 2025/38 laying down measures to strengthen solidarity and capacities in the Union to detect, prepare for and respond to cyber threats and incidents and amending Regulation (EU) 2021/694 (Cyber Solidarity Act)

Official text: Regulation (EU) 2025/38 of 19 December 2024 laying down measures to strengthen solidarity and capacities in the Union to detect, prepare for and respond to cyber threats and incidents and amending Regulation (EU) 2021/694 (Cyber Solidarity Act) (OJ L 2025/38, 15.1.2025)Tier 1 · primary law

Status
In force as of 27 October 2026
Key dates
1 dated event
Competent authority
not established in this dataset
Sanction ceiling
no amount recorded

In force since 4 February 2025, the twentieth day after publication (Art. 26; OJ L 2025/38, 15.1.2025), with no separate application date. It also amends Regulation (EU) 2021/694 (Art. 22). Read on 27 Oct 2026 in the Official Journal text retrieved from the Publications Office's Cellar; the Publications Office's metadata records it in force from that date.

In short: what you need to know

  • Objective: Union capacities to detect, prepare for and respond to cyber threats and incidents: a European Cybersecurity Alert System of national and cross-border cyber hubs, a Cybersecurity Emergency Mechanism with an EU Cybersecurity Reserve, and a European Cybersecurity Incident Review Mechanism.
  • Who it binds: Member State · Public authority
  • Who it protects: not established
  • Core obligations: not established key provisions →
  • Key dates: Entry into force 4 February 2025 the timeline →
  • Sanction ceiling: no amount recordedNone: no provision of the Regulation sets fines or penalties (the Official Journal text, searched in full on 27 Oct 2026, contains neither word). enforcement →

What does the Cyber Solidarity Act do?

Union capacities to detect, prepare for and respond to cyber threats and incidents: a European Cybersecurity Alert System of national and cross-border cyber hubs, a Cybersecurity Emergency Mechanism with an EU Cybersecurity Reserve, and a European Cybersecurity Incident Review Mechanism.

What does the Cyber Solidarity Act require? Key provisions

3 provisions recorded. This is what the dataset holds, not the whole instrument — an article that is not here has not been entered, which is a different statement from its not existing.

ArticleHeadingBindsApplies
Art. 3Establishment of the European Cybersecurity Alert SystemA pan-European network of National Cyber Hubs and Cross-Border Cyber Hubs, joining on a voluntary basis, is established to enhance the Union's detection, analysis and data-processing capabilities in relation to cyber threats and the prevention of incidents (3(1)). A Member State that decides to participate designates or establishes a National Cyber Hub (Art. 4(1)). The actions are funded from the Digital Europe Programme (3(3)).not recordedno application date recorded for this article
Art. 14Establishment of the EU Cybersecurity ReserveAn EU Cybersecurity Reserve of response services from trusted managed security service providers assists its users, upon request, in responding to and initiating recovery from significant, large-scale or large-scale-equivalent cybersecurity incidents (14(1)–(2)). Its users are Member States' cyber crisis management authorities and CSIRTs, CERT-EU, and competent authorities of third countries associated to the Digital Europe Programme (14(3)). The Commission has overall responsibility for its implementation (14(4)).European Commissionno application date recorded for this article
Art. 21European Cybersecurity Incident Review MechanismAt the request of the Commission or EU-CyCLONe, ENISA, with the support of the CSIRTs network and the approval of the Member States concerned, reviews and assesses a specific significant or large-scale cybersecurity incident and delivers an incident review report to EU-CyCLONe, the CSIRTs network, the Member States concerned and the Commission (21(1)). The report may draw recommendations (21(4)), and ENISA may issue a publicly available version (21(5)).ENISAno application date recorded for this article

How does the Cyber Solidarity Act interact with other EU laws?

1 recorded interaction with other instruments — each with a direction, the provisions that carry it and its own sources. Direction is preserved as recorded: an instrument that amends another is not the same as one amended by it.

NIS2 Enables Cyber Solidarity Act

The other instrument's provisions operate through definitions, bodies, means or populations this instrument establishes, and say so. Recorded only on an express reference in the DEPENDENT instrument's text; the locator is in that text. Added 27 Oct 2026.

The Cyber Solidarity Act defines CSIRTs, entities, the entities of sectors of high criticality and other critical sectors, risk, incident, significant and large-scale cybersecurity incidents and managed security service providers by reference to NIS2.
